notes:
Context: Threadline builds an in-IDE copilot for professional developers (VS Code + JetBrains plugin). Primary KPI = perceived responsiveness. Key asks: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) <= 120ms on typical dev machines, end-to-end jitter <30ms, and deterministic fallbacks when numbers spike.

Workload specifics:
- Interaction pattern: keystroke-triggered completions (short, often 5-80 tokens), occasional multi-line refactors (200-800 tokens).
- High fanout: single API key used across orgs; need per-route token budgets to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Metrics: measure per-keystroke TTFT distribution (p50/p95/p99), jitter histogram, bytes-per-chunk, and perceived typing latency.

Performance constraints discussed:
- Customer measured baseline (internal LLM) first-token ~220ms in EU region; target is <120ms in NA region for hosted path. They want Redwood to provide recommendations: model varants (smaller quantized for keystroke vs larger for refactor), kernel choices, and batching windows.
- Backpressure: editor-level throttling desired. They want Redwood to support explicit client hints (e.g., low-latency flag) to prioritize per-key streams and reduce batching delay.
- Token budget tuning: prefer default per-completion budget 64 tokens with automatic soft-fallback to 32 tokens when concurrency high. Request Redwood Optimize suggestions for cost/TTFT tradeoffs.

Security & deployment:
- Must support SSO (SAML), audit logs retained 1 year, KMS-managed keys for any persisted artifacts.
- Prefer Dedicated pool inside VPC for evaluation (data residency + egress controls).

Product asks & acceptance criteria:
- Show a POC run with a dedicated pool that meets TTFT <120ms p50 and <180ms p95 in our lab; jitter p95 <40ms.
- Expose SDK hooks for: immediate partial flush (small chunks), incremental token accounting, and a backpressure error code so the frontend can gracefully stall inline completion.
- Model/version pinning UI + API: ability to pin keystroke-model and refactor-model independently.
- Cost visibility: token-level cost for streaming sessions and per-route budgets.

Quotes / paraphrases from calls:
- "Perceived latency beats throughput for 80% of sessions — if the first token feels instant, users accept slower tails." — Head of Product
- "We need deterministic behavior when latency spikes; fallback to smaller model or cached completions is preferred to random timeouts." — Staff SW Eng

- Best default chunk size for streaming to balance RTT vs CPU (client suggested 8-16 token chunks).
- Autoscaling/burst cost model for spikes during team-wide refactors (bulk completions).
